newsitem.title: HONG KONG: San Miguel HK shares hit year low.
newsitem.headline: San Miguel HK shares hit year low.

text.p: San Miguel Brewery Hong Kong Ltd (SMBHK) shares hit a year-low late Friday morning after the company's parent abandoned a privatisation bid, brokers said.
SMBHK fell HK$0.185 or 5.6 percent to HK$3.10 when trade in the shares resumed on Friday after being suspended on Tuesday.
The company said on Friday its controlling shareholder, Neptunia Corp Ltd, had abandoned its proposal to privatise the company after the price proposed by Neptunia was deemed too low.
Neptunia, a unit of food and drink giant San Miguel Corp, had approached the company in October with a possible privatisation offer at HK$3.75 per share.
Neptunia holds about 64 percent of SMBHK.

Nikko Securities Co's Kent Rossiter said the gap between the privatisation price and its recent trading price might mean "maybe there was not a lot of confidence the deal was going to go through in the first place".
Stephen Brown, research director at NAVA SC, said the stock was very illiquid, and SMBHK was not a growth business.

SMBHK also said the Takeovers and Mergers Executive would review and make further enquiries into all matters relating to the possible privatisation offer to see whether relevant rules had been fully complied with. -- H.K. newsroom (852) 2843 6370
